claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2022-08-25 reports: Ramotswa households had more formal employment and livelihood diversity, and greater capacity to withstand drought and flood shocks than Xhumaga, but faced dry taps, billing, maintenance and outage barriers.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Qualitative/quasi-random two-site comparison; socioeconomic differences and water-system administration are not an isolated climate-adaptation treatment effect.

gaps: Human-wildlife conflict is not equated with FCV. No complete source-supported climate-to-interpersonal/armed-conflict or reverse-FCV pathway is assembled.
Dated compensation grievances and co-located social exclusion warrant sensitivity in programme design but do not establish a climate-caused conflict chain.

executive_assessment.text: Named evidence distinguishes drought-vulnerability pockets in Southern/Kgalagadi/western Ghanzi and flood/poverty overlap around Ngamiland Delta and Francistown.

Xhumaga and Ramotswa cases show different water-access, gender and livelihood constraints. Wildlife exposure and infrastructure failures are retained without being relabelled as interpersonal violence.
Dated drought monitoring, relief options and compensation grievances identify institutional issues. Climate/social-exclusion co-location and human-wildlife conflict are not complete FCV mechanisms.
